She exulted in her new freedom.

words.def_en: to show or prove that something is true
examples: The letters attest to his patience.
His work attests his skill.

words.def_en: too ready to believe what people say
examples: The gullible buyer paid twice the price.
Scams target gullible people.

words.def_en: to move soldiers into position, or to put to use
examples: They deployed extra staff at the gate.
Troops were deployed along the border.

words.def_en: something or someone very hard to understand
examples: His reasons remain an enigma.
The enigma of the missing keys deepened.

words.def_en: unsuccessful because it stops before finishing
examples: They made an abortive attempt to climb.
The abortive talks ended in silence.

words.def_en: to change something slightly
examples: We modified the design to save weight.
The rules were modified last year.

words.def_en: to provide room for, or to change in order to fit
examples: The hall can accommodate three hundred.
He accommodated his plans to hers.

words.def_en: happening naturally without planning
examples: There was spontaneous applause.
Her offer was entirely spontaneous.

words.def_en: present from birth rather than learned
examples: He has an innate sense of timing.
Curiosity seems innate in children.

words.def_en: a thin covering, or a polite surface hiding the truth
examples: The table has a walnut veneer.
A veneer of calm hid his anger.

words.def_en: a very great number of
examples: The sky was full of myriad stars.
Myriad details fill the report.

words.def_en: polite and confident in a sophisticated way
examples: Her urbane manner put everyone at ease.
He is an urbane and witty host.

words.def_en: to want something very strongly
examples: He craved a cup of tea.
Children crave attention from their parents.

words.def_en: not connected with the subject
examples: That question is irrelevant here.
He dismissed the point as irrelevant.

words.def_en: to consider something to be true or of a quality
examples: They deem the plan too risky.
The building was deemed unsafe.

words.def_en: existing as a natural part of something
examples: There are inherent risks in the sport.
She has an inherent distrust of crowds.

words.def_en: a person very interested in a subject
examples: A film buff recommended the classic.
Only a train buff would notice that.

words.def_en: to play noisily and happily
examples: The puppies romp in the garden.
The children romped through the snow.

words.def_en: existing but not yet active or visible
examples: Her latent talent surprised the coach.
The defect stayed latent for years.

words.def_en: winding, or complicated and long
examples: A tortuous road leads to the village.
The negotiations were tortuous.

words.def_en: travelling from place to place
examples: An itinerant seller visits each spring.
He led an itinerant life for years.

words.def_en: a long journey or wandering
examples: His peregrination took three years.
The book describes her peregrinations.

words.def_en: relating to marriage
examples: They value their conjugal life.
The visit was a conjugal one.

words.def_en: an instrument for air pressure, or a sign of change
examples: The barometer fell before the storm.
Sales are a barometer of confidence.

words.def_en: a false belief that you are extremely powerful
examples: His megalomania grew with each success.
The film mocks the ruler's megalomania.

words.def_en: wasting money or resources carelessly
examples: Profligate spending ruined the club.
The plan is profligate with water.

words.def_en: serious disagreement or fighting
examples: Industrial strife closed the plant.
Family strife troubled him for years.

words.def_en: very many in number
examples: Their reasons were legion.
Problems were legion after the flood.

words.def_en: a sudden seizure of power, or a clever success
examples: The army staged a coup at dawn.
Signing the star was a marketing coup.

words.def_en: an official pardon for a group of people
examples: The government declared an amnesty.
Prisoners were freed under the amnesty.

words.def_en: a person living outside their own country
examples: The city has a large expatriate community.
Many expatriates returned after the war.

words.def_en: to clear someone of blame officially
examples: The review exonerated the pilot.
New evidence exonerated two men.

words.def_en: an official order given without discussion
examples: The change was made by fiat.
A fiat closed the market overnight.

words.def_en: telling lies, or untrue
examples: The mendacious report misled the public.
He gave a mendacious account.

words.def_en: extremely unwilling to spend money
examples: Their parsimonious budget starved the lab.
He was parsimonious even with paper.

words.def_en: relating to money
examples: She had a pecuniary interest in the sale.
The dispute was pecuniary, not personal.

words.def_en: to take something apart, or to end a system
examples: They dismantled the stage in an hour.
The scheme was quietly dismantled.

words.def_en: costly and impressive
examples: They served a sumptuous dinner.
The sumptuous hall glittered.

words.def_en: to agree to pay the costs of something
examples: A bank underwrote the exhibition.
The fund underwrites the repairs.

words.def_en: limiting what people can do
examples: The rules are too restrictive.
He found the dress code restrictive.

words.def_en: not sharp, or saying things very directly
examples: The knife was blunt and useless.
She gave a blunt answer.

words.def_en: a warm sad longing for the past
examples: The song filled him with nostalgia.
Nostalgia for the old shop brought her back.

words.def_en: widespread, especially of something bad
examples: Rumour was rife in the office.
Corruption was rife at that time.

words.def_en: to refuse to do something or go on
examples: The horse balked at the stream.
He balked at paying the deposit.

words.def_en: to criticise someone in angry and insulting terms
examples: The press reviled him for months.
Critics reviled the film, but it sold.

words.def_en: showing a low opinion of someone
examples: He made a derogatory comment about her accent.
Avoid derogatory language in the report.

words.def_en: to charge someone officially with a crime
examples: A grand jury indicted two officers.
The report indicts the whole system.

words.def_en: unclear and not well defined
examples: Their plans were still nebulous.
He gave a nebulous promise.

words.def_en: annoying and hard to get rid of
examples: Those pesky flies ruined the picnic.
A pesky detail delayed the launch.

words.def_en: smelling strongly of something, or bringing it to mind
examples: The kitchen was redolent of coffee.
The name is redolent of summer holidays.

words.def_en: eating both plants and meat, or interested in everything
examples: Pigs are omnivorous animals.
She is an omnivorous reader.

words.def_en: very different from each other
examples: They tried to unite disparate groups.
The study mixes disparate data.

words.def_en: not eating or drinking too much
examples: He leads an abstemious life.
Her abstemious habits kept her healthy.

words.def_en: a state of quiet rest
examples: The garden is a place of repose.
She lay in gentle repose.

words.def_en: still existing, especially of old things
examples: Only three copies are extant.
The extant letters fill two volumes.

words.def_en: the unexpected changes in a situation or life
examples: The vicissitudes of the market ruined him.
She weathered the vicissitudes of travel.

words.def_en: a large building, or a complex system
examples: The edifice dominates the square.
They built a whole edifice of rules.

words.def_en: unpleasantly hot and humid
examples: A sultry afternoon kept everyone indoors.
The sultry air hung over the city.

words.def_en: expressed strongly and clearly
examples: She wrote a trenchant criticism.
His trenchant remarks ended the debate.

words.def_en: having great power or influence
examples: A puissant trade union blocked the plan.
The puissant family owned the port.

words.def_en: continuing at full strength
examples: The storm continued unabated.
Demand for tickets went on unabated.

words.def_en: silly and tearful from too much emotion
examples: He became maudlin after a few drinks.
The ending is maudlin rather than moving.

words.def_en: humour at a time when it is not suitable
examples: There was no room for levity at the funeral.
His levity offended the family.

words.def_en: looking or sounding very sad
examples: He spoke in a lugubrious voice.
The lugubrious music matched the rain.
